title: Adaptive SLO budget rebalancer and initiative priority grid
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
Build an adaptive error-budget rebalancer + initiative priority grid that automatically suggests reallocations of error budget pools across product initiatives each cycle, and surfaces trade-offs in a visual grid in Console. The goal is to move from manual, spreadsheet-heavy reassignments to a repeatable, observable system that: (1) forecasts burn trajectories, (2) simulates reallocation outcomes, and (3) produces a recommended priority order for initiatives tied to OKRs and SLO tolerance.

Why now:
- We repeatedly saw month-to-month firefighting where teams either overspend error budget or hoard it, causing inefficient allocation and missed product experiments.
- Several incidents in Q4 2025 exposed that manual reallocation decisions were delayed during high burn, increasing customer impact.

Goals (success metrics):
- Time-to-decision for budget reallocation reduced from ~3 days to < 4 hours for on-call+PM review.
- 80% of recommended reallocations accepted by initiative owners in pilot cohort.
- Reduce number of emergency rollbacks by 35% quarter-over-quarter.
- Make a visible confidence band for burn forecasts (50/90 percentile) in Console.

Scope (MVP):
- Aggregation of initiative-level SLIs, current error-budget balance, and burn-rate trends.
- Simulation engine that runs 3 allocation scenarios (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and projects SLI attainment and incident probability over the next 30 days.
- Priority grid UI in Console with sortable columns: initiative importance (OKR weight), projected SLO risk, business criticality, and recommended reallocation action.
- Audit log for every reallocation recommendation and final decision (links to rollout PR/incident if applicable).

Out of scope for MVP:
- Automated auto-enforcement of reallocations (we will only recommend; manual approval required).
- Cross-organization chargeback billing changes in finance systems (integration is a follow-up).

User stories:
- As a Platform PM, I want to see a ranked list of initiatives that are most at risk of burning SLOs and what % of budget to shift to lower-risk mitigation initiatives, so I can advise leadership quickly.
- As an Initiative Owner, I want to run a what-if simulation for a proposed increase in traffic (x2) to see potential error-budget exhaustion date and required mitigation.
- As an Oncall Lead, I want an audit trail showing why a reallocation was recommended so I can justify rollback decisions post-incident.

Acceptance criteria:
- Aggregated SLI + error-budget data present for pilot initiatives (>= 6 teams).
- Simulation runs in < 30s for a 30-day projection on typical dataset.
- Console UI displays recommendations and links to a runbook/GitHub PR.
- Audit log entry created for each recommendation with timestamp and decision.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Data ingestion: Define minimal SLI schema and export connector (Data team).
- Simulation engine: Lightweight stochastic burn model (Noah Kim + Eng) with adjustable assumptions (traffic delta, mitigation lead time).
- Decision heuristics: Multi-factor scoring combining OKR weight, SLI risk (time-to-exhaustion), and customer impact. Weights will be configurable.
- UI: Priority grid and simulation modal in Console (Design: Eve Zhang).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Internal alpha with Platform and Reliability teams; collect feedback.
- Week 3: Pilot with 6 customer-facing initiatives (one team per org).
- Week 6: Evaluate pilot acceptance metrics and adjust heuristics.

Monitoring, dashboards, and alerts:
- Grafana dashboard: Initiative heatmap (current burn, projected exhaustion date, recommendation).
- Alert: If recommended reallocation would still leave an initiative with <7 days of budget under worst-case scenario, send high-priority alert to SRE + Initiative Owner.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Poor model assumptions lead to wrong recommendations. Mitigation: Include confidence bands and show underlying assumptions to users; initial conservative defaults.
- Risk: Initiative owners distrust automated recommendations. Mitigation: Keep manual approval and provide clear audit trail + easy simulation replay.

Open questions:
- Should finance be able to tag budgets as "non-transferable"? (Design & Legal input required)
- Minimum granularity for an initiative (team, product area, microservice)? Proposal: initiative-level only for MVP.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (PM), Liam O'Connor (TPM)
- Eng: Sofia Martinez (Eng Lead), Noah Kim (Data Scientist), Priya Rao (Backend)
- Design: Eve Zhang
- SRE/Oncall: Marcus Liu

Notes & trade-offs recorded:
- We chose recommendation-only vs automatic enforcement to preserve organizational trust; enforcement will be revisited if adoption and accuracy exceed thresholds.
- We model burn stochastically rather than deterministically to surface tail risks; this increases compute cost but gives better risk signals.

2026-01-20 Sofia Martinez: Engineering spike completed. Preliminary burn model implemented; stochastic simulation prototype shows plausible projections. CPU cost estimate ~0.5 core per run when batched.
2026-01-26 Eve Zhang: First mockups reviewed. UX decision: show three recommended allocation scenarios with an explanation tooltip for each. Design requests example copy for confidence bands.
2026-01-30 Liam O'Connor: Scoped pilot cohort (6 initiatives) and scheduled alpha demo for 2026-02-03. Data connector schema v0.1 approved (see Confluence).
2026-02-03 Noah Kim: Pilot data ingestion completed for 6 teams. Simulation latency optimized to ~18s. Still need to tighten false-positive rate for high-risk recommendations.
